issues.display_title: Issue #1966: Generate Batch Invoice PDFs and Provide ZIP Archive for user_id = 2853
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

Invoices are currently generated on-demand when clicked individually in the UI, making it impractical for users with large transaction histories to download them one by one. Run a script to batch generate all PDF invoices for user_id = 2853 and package them into a single .zip file for delivery.

Implementation & Verification Result (2026-09-28)

1. Implementation Summary

  • Pull Request: #1970 (Merged to main)
  • Endpoint: POST /v2/support/invoices/generate
  • Architecture (Domain-based ADR):
    • BatchGenerateInvoicesController: Handles HTTP payload, parameters, and dual-response dispatching.
    • BatchGenerateInvoicesAction: HTTP-free domain action coordinating validation, DB queries, PDF generation, and ZIP packaging.
    • BatchGenerateInvoicesValidator: Validates target_user_id and query limits.
    • SuperUserValidator: Restricts operator access strictly to support operators with user_type == 2 and listed in SUPER_USER.
    • SupportInvoiceRepository: Retrieves successful purchase transactions (result = '0') from ccdb.cc_purchase.
    • InvoiceZipService: Packages generated PDF receipts into a clean ZIP archive via native PHP ZipArchive.

2. Supported Parameters & Dual Modes

Parameter Type Default Description
target_user_id integer required Target user ID whose invoices are to be compiled
limit integer null (all) Optional batch size limit
force boolean false If true, re-generates existing PDFs on disk
download boolean false If true, streams ZIP binary directly (BinaryFileResponse); if false, returns JSON response envelope with zip_url

3. Verification & Testing

  • Automated Tests: 41 PHPUnit unit/integration tests passing (80 assertions, 100% pass).
  • Local Verification:
    • Operator: adamnurdin01@gmail.com (user_id = 12068, user_type = 2).
    • Target User: muhamad.rifky.dev@gmail.com (user_id = 50214).
    • Execution: 5 invoices compiled into /data/moderation/50214/receipt/ and packaged into invoices_50214.zip (128 KB, 5 files verified).
    • Both JSON response envelope and direct binary ZIP streaming download verified working with HTTP 200 OK.
  • Production Audit (user_id = 2853):
    • 122 total successful transactions audited (44 existing PDFs, 78 pending compilation).
    • Endpoint is ready on main branch to execute on production server apil-1.
    • Zip File: https://apil.gothru.co/invoice/2853/receipt/invoices_2853.zip

issues.display_title: Issue #1971: feat(panoramas): Add Batch Update Panorama Locations API
issues.main_description_html:
Context

Batch update endpoint for MapThru (and internal services) to update panorama coordinates (lat, lng) in a single atomic transaction without requiring user JWT tokens.

Specification

  • Method & Path: PUT /v1/internal/panoramas/locations/batch & POST /v1/internal/panoramas/locations/batch
  • Middleware: internal-api-key (header: Internal-API-Key: {key})
  • Response Format: Plain JSON standard (ResponseEnvelopeHelper::responseMessages)

Request Payload:

{
  "tour_key": "oOT5kHaV",
  "locations": [
    { "pano_id": 47890269, "lat": -6.5745312, "lng": 107.7958160 },
    { "pano_id": 47890270, "lat": -6.5746251, "lng": 107.7956760 }
  ]
}

Response Payload:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "messages": "Panorama locations updated successfully",
    "updated_count": 2
  }
}

Acceptance Criteria

  • Client can batch update panorama coordinates using tour_key.
  • Protected by internal-api-key middleware (no user JWT required).
  • Moderation ID resolved from tour_key (409 tour_not_found if invalid).
  • Database persistence is atomic (2_lat, 3_lng updated, date_updated touched).
  • Unit / Action tests passing 100%.

Result Summary

  • Implementation: Domain-Based ADR endpoint at PUT & POST /v1/internal/panoramas/locations/batch protected by internal-api-key. Coordinates are updated atomically on 4_panoramas and moderation date_updated is refreshed.
  • Testing: 100% test coverage across DTO, Validator, Action, Controller, Repository, and Routes (253 tests passing).
  • PR: #1972 (initial), #1973 (refactor to tour_key & internal-api-key, merged).

issues.display_title: Issue #1974: fix(invoice): handle missing billing address gracefully during invoice generation
issues.main_description_html:
Description

When a user unlocks a hosted overlay (or goes through any one-time payment / subscription flow triggering invoice generation), a fatal unhandled exception occurred if the user had not previously saved their billing address details.

Root Cause

In InvoiceHelper::generateInvoicePdf() and BillingClass::generateInvoiceV2(), billing information was retrieved using:

$billingInfo = $this->databaseClass->tableBillingAddress()->where('user_id', $userId)->get();
$billingInfo = json_decode(json_encode($billingInfo), true);
$billingInfo = $billingInfo[0];

When no row exists in billing_address for the user, $billingInfo evaluates to an empty array []. Accessing index 0 throws:

ErrorException: Undefined array key 0

Solution

  1. Replaced get() with first() to retrieve a single record cleanly.
  2. Added a graceful fallback: if no billing address record is found, user name (first_name, last_name) and country are retrieved directly from the users table, setting empty string fallbacks for street address, city, state, postal code, and company name.
  3. Added PHPUnit test coverage (InvoiceHelperBillingFallbackTest) simulating users with missing billing address entries.

Result

  • Commit: 9bebff7078a67d451683f47080861d441cba3c01 pushed directly to main.
  • Affected Tour Verified: Tour pziWHtJt (user_id 16127) activated successfully in overlay_audit.
  • Test Evidence:

PHPUnit 9.6.34 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.

Time: 00:06.852, Memory: 102.55 MB

OK (1 test, 1 assertion)

issues.display_title: Issue #1950: PayPal Upgrade: align path with SUBSCRIBE (webhook-first + SSE)
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Update the PayPal plan upgrade process to use the webhook-first workflow, matching the standard subscription flow. Instead of relying on client-side capture requests, upgrades are processed securely via the PayPal webhook with real-time status updates delivered through Server-Sent Events (SSE).

Objectives

  • Save upgrade details upon subscription creation so the webhook has the full upgrade context.
  • Finalize the plan upgrade (cancel previous subscription and activate new plan) directly during webhook processing.
  • Broadcast real-time status updates to the frontend via SSE.
  • Keep the capture endpoint strictly as a safe, idempotent fallback.

Pull Request

issues.display_title: Issue #1975: feat(auth): support Keycloak Bearer token in Authenticate middleware for external ecosystem apps
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Enable the auth route middleware (App\Http\Middleware\Authenticate) to natively verify and accept standard Keycloak OIDC Access Tokens (Authorization: Bearer <token>). This allows sibling apps in the GoThru ecosystem (such as Panorra, mobile apps, or internal microservices) to call GoThru API endpoints directly using their Keycloak SSO identity without needing custom token-exchange roundtrips or legacy gt. tokens.

Background & Problem

  • Currently, Authenticate.php only accepts legacy internal tokens formatted as gt.<jwt> signed with symmetric HS256 (KEY_TOKEN).
  • External ecosystem products like Panorra authenticate users directly against Keycloak SSO and receive RS256-signed Keycloak access tokens.
  • Sibling apps are currently forced to execute an extra login exchange (POST /v1/auth/keycloak-login) or bypass authentication entirely on certain endpoints.

Proposed Changes

  1. Dual-Driver Token Classifier in Authenticate.php:

    • Inspect the Authorization header.
    • Strip leading Bearer prefix if present.
    • If token begins with gt., route to the existing legacy handler (checkToken / KEY_TOKEN).
    • If token is a Keycloak JWT, route to the Keycloak validation handler.

  2. Keycloak Verification Driver:

    • Verify RS256 signature using the Keycloak realm JWKS endpoint via KeycloakTokenHelper::verifyAndGetClaims() (cached in Redis for 1 hour).
    • Validate realm issuer (KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL/realms/{realm}).
    • Validate authorized party (azp) or audience (aud) against configured KEYCLOAK_ALLOWED_CLIENTS.

  3. User Resolution & JIT Provisioning:

    • Lookup existing user by keycloak_sub.
    • Fallback to matching by email and link keycloak_sub to the user record.
    • If user does not exist in GoThru and email_verified === true, JIT provision user profile and defaults via KeycloakUserRegistrar::register().

  4. Request Enrichment (Backward Compatibility):

    • Merge user_id, subscribtion, and user_data into $request so all downstream controllers function without code changes.

  5. Configuration Update:

    • Update KEYCLOAK_ALLOWED_CLIENTS in environment configuration to include client identifiers for Panorra (e.g. gothru-dashboard,panorra,panorra-app,app-gothru-local).

  6. Automated Tests:

    • Add unit/feature tests for Authenticate middleware covering valid Keycloak tokens, expired tokens, untrusted clients, missing user cases, and request attribute injection.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Requests bearing a valid Keycloak access token with an allowed client ID (e.g., Panorra) are accepted by all routes protected by middleware => 'auth'.
  • Downstream controllers receive consistent $request->user_id, $request->subscribtion, and $request->user_data.
  • Legacy gt. tokens continue to work identically with zero regression for GoThru Dashboard.
  • Expired, untrusted client, or tampered Keycloak tokens are rejected with HTTP 401.
  • Unit and route tests pass cleanly.

Result

🚀 Implementation Deliverables

  • Pull Request: #1976 (Merged into main).
  • Key Files & Changes:
    • app/Http/Middleware/Authenticate.php: Hybrid dual-driver auth middleware with native Keycloak RS256 Bearer token support alongside legacy gt.<jwt> tokens.
    • app/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakUserResolver.php: Extracted shared user resolution, auto-linking (keycloak_sub), and JIT provisioning helper.
    • app/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakTokenHelper.php: Added panorra and panorra-app to default allowed Keycloak clients.
    • app/Actions/Auth/KeycloakLoginAction.php: Refactored to delegate user resolution to KeycloakUserResolver.

🔬 Automated Testing & Verification

  • Unit Test Suites:
    • tests/Http/Middleware/AuthenticateTest.php: 16/16 tests passed (100%).
    • tests/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakUserResolverTest.php: 7/7 tests passed (100%).
    • tests/Helpers/Auth/KeycloakTokenHelperTest.php: 7/7 tests passed (100%).
  • Live E2E Verification (verified on protected endpoint /users/detail with user muhamad.rifky.dev@gmail.com / User ID: 50214):
    • Legacy gt.<jwt> token with and without Bearer prefix: 200 OK.
    • Keycloak RS256 Bearer token (panorra & gothru-dashboard clients): 200 OK (auto-linked keycloak_sub).
    • Security negative tests (expired token, unauthorized client, unverified email, account linking conflict, rogue signature): all rejected with 401 Unauthorized.

issues.display_title: Issue #1977: refactor(routes): remove dead and obsolete routes pointing to non-existent controller methods
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

During a comprehensive routing table audit, 16 registered routes were identified whose target controller methods no longer exist. If invoked, these endpoints fail with a 500 Fatal Error (ReflectionException: Method ... does not exist in class ...). Cross-checks confirmed that none of these endpoints are called by gothru-dashboard or any active client.

Dead Routes to Remove

  1. routes/web.php

    • GET /streetview-publish -> User\UserController@addAccountGooglePlus
    • POST /billings/create-customer -> User\BillingController@createCustomer (including obsolete billings group)

  2. routes/tourRoutes.php

    • GET /tours/ -> Tours\ToursController@getallTours (under legacy // Function not found block)
    • GET /tours/search -> Tours\ToursController@searchTour
    • GET /tours/list-monthly -> Tours\ToursController@listToursMonthly
    • GET /tours/recents -> Tours\ToursController@listRecentTours
    • GET /tours/stats -> Tours\ToursController@getStatsTour
    • GET /tours/v1/publish-status-processing-maps -> Tours\PublishController@publishStatusProcessingInGoogleMapsV1
    • POST /tours/v1/publish-status-processing-links -> Tours\PublishController@publishStatusProcessingInGoogleLinksV1
    • POST /tours/stitching -> Tours\ToursController@autoStiching
    • GET /tours/stitching -> Tours\ToursController@getStitchingStatus
    • GET /tours/debug-sv-info/{mid} -> Tours\PublishController@debugSVInfo

  3. routes/billingRoutes.php

    • POST /billing/stripe -> User\BillingController@addPayment
    • GET /billing/product -> User\BillingController@getProductDetail
    • GET /billing/subs-capture -> User\BillingController@captureSubsPaypal
    • GET /billing/order-capture -> User\BillingController@captureOrderPaypal

Tasks

  • Remove obsolete route definitions from routes/web.php, routes/tourRoutes.php, and routes/billingRoutes.php.
  • Re-sync docs/REGISTERED_APIS.md and audit documentation.
  • Verify routing table integrity (confirm 0 missing method reflection exceptions).

Result

Implementation Evidence

  • Pull Request: #1978
  • Commit: 5bcb8e8ea
  • Files Modified:
    • routes/web.php (removed 2 dead routes and empty billings group)
    • routes/tourRoutes.php (removed 9 dead routes, cleaned legacy comment block)
    • routes/billingRoutes.php (removed 4 dead routes)
    • docs/REGISTERED_APIS.md (re-synced total count to 682 routes)
    • tests/Routes/DeadRoutesCleanedIntegrityTest.php (added automated route reflection integrity test)

Verification & Testing Evidence

  • Automated Integrity Test: tests/Routes/DeadRoutesCleanedIntegrityTest.php
    • test_all_registered_routes_have_valid_controller_actions: Verified all 682 active registered routes point to existing controller classes and callable methods (0 missing methods).
    • test_cleaned_dead_routes_are_not_registered: Verified all 15 deleted route paths return null in the routing table.
  • Route Test Suite: Ran ./vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Routes — 48/48 tests passed (100%), 139 assertions, 0 failures.
  • Frontend Impact: Full codebase grep across gothru-dashboard confirmed 0 references to any of the 15 removed endpoints.
